faq.description: Everything you need to know about studying dentistry abroad, BDS, licensing, salaries, family settlement and career pathways.

items.question: Can I study BDS abroad as an Indian student?
items.answer: Yes — many countries offer dental degrees in English-medium programmes. We help you choose a recognised university aligned to your goals.

items.question: What about Dental Hygiene or other dental courses?
items.answer: We also guide students toward dental hygiene, therapy and technology programmes abroad — distinct allied dental roles with different study and registration pathways.

items.question: Will I be able to practise abroad after my dental degree?
items.answer: Usually only after clearing the destination country's licensing or registration requirements, such as ORE in the UK, ADC in Australia, NDEB in Canada or INBDE plus advanced-standing study in the USA. English requirements may also apply.

items.question: What do dentists earn abroad?
items.answer: Dentist salaries vary widely by country, experience, practice type, location and year. The salary table on this page provides illustrative averages, not guarantees.

items.question: Can I settle abroad with my family as a dentist?
items.answer: Several countries offer skilled-worker and dependent-visa pathways that may lead toward settlement, subject to eligibility and current immigration rules.

items.question: Is the dental licensing process hard?
items.answer: For foreign-trained dentists it can be demanding, lengthy and competitive. This is why we encourage students to understand licensing requirements before choosing their study destination.

items.question: Do I need NEET for BDS abroad?
items.answer: Depending on the pathway and recognition requirements, NEET may be required for Indian students. We confirm the current rules for your chosen route.

items.question: How long is a dental degree abroad?
items.answer: BDS, DDS and DMD programmes are commonly around 5 years including clinical training, while allied dental courses can be shorter depending on the programme and country.

items.question: Is English mandatory?
items.answer: English requirements depend on the programme and destination. For many overseas licensing pathways, English tests such as IELTS or OET may be required.

items.question: Do you guarantee a job, visa or licence?
items.answer: No. We provide honest, organised and end-to-end guidance, but jobs, visas, licensing and registration outcomes are decided by employers and authorities.

items.question: Which country is best for dentistry?
items.answer: There is no single best country. It depends on your academic profile, budget, career goals and where you ultimately want to practise and settle.

items.question: How do I start?
items.answer: Book a free counselling session. We will understand your goals and share a personalised dental-career roadmap with no obligation.
